483:     base : array-like of int
484:         The base positions of each label
485: 
486:     ticks : array-like of string
487:         The labels for the ticks
488:     """
489: 
490:     def __init__(self, base, ticks):
491:         self._map = {int(k): v for k, v in zip(base, ticks)}
492: 
493:     def __call__(self, x, pos=None):
494:         """Map the input position to its corresponding interval label"""
495:         return self._map.get(int(x), "")
496: 
497: 
498: def hierarchy(intervals_hier, labels_hier, levels=None, ax=None, **kwargs):
499:     """Plot a hierarchical segmentation
500: 
501:     Parameters
502:     ----------
503:     intervals_hier : list of np.ndarray
504:         A list of segmentation intervals.  Each element should be
505:         an n-by-2 array of segment intervals, in the format returned by
506:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_intervals` or
507:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
508:         Segmentations should be ordered by increasing specificity.
509:     labels_hier : list of list-like
510:         A list of segmentation labels.  Each element should
511:         be a list of labels for the corresponding element in
512:         `intervals_hier`.
513:     levels : list of string
514:         Each element ``levels[i]`` is a label for the ```i`` th segmentation.
515:         This is used in the legend to denote the levels in a segment hierarchy.
516:     ax : matplotlib.pyplot.axes
517:         An axis handle on which to draw the intervals.
518:         If none is provided, a new set of axes is created.
519:     **kwargs
520:         Additional keyword arguments to `labeled_intervals`.
521: 
522:     Returns
523:     -------
524:     ax : matplotlib.pyplot.axes._subplots.AxesSubplot
525:         A handle to the (possibly constructed) plot axes
526:     """
527:     # This will break if a segment label exists in multiple levels
528:     if levels is None:
529:         levels = list(range(len(intervals_hier)))
530: 
531:     # Get the axes handle
532:     ax, _ = __get_axes(ax=ax)
533: 
534:     # Count the pre-existing patches
535:     n_patches = len(ax.patches)
536: 
537:     for ints, labs, key in zip(intervals_hier[::-1], labels_hier[::-1], levels[::-1]):
538:         labeled_intervals(ints, labs, label=key, ax=ax, **kwargs)
539: 
540:     return ax
541: 
542: 
543: def events(
544:     times,
545:     labels=None,
546:     base=None,
547:     height=None,
548:     ax=None,
549:     text_kw=None,
550:     prop_cycle=None,
551:     **kwargs,
552: ):
553:     """Plot event times as a set of vertical lines
554: 
555:     Parameters
556:     ----------
557:     times : np.ndarray, shape=(n,)
558:         event times, in the format returned by
559:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_events` or
560:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_events`.
561:     labels : list, shape=(n,), optional
562:         event labels, in the format returned by
563:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_events`.
564:     base : number
565:         The vertical position of the base of the line.
566:         By default, this will be the bottom of the plot.
567:     height : number
568:         The height of the lines.
569:         By default, this will be the top of the plot (minus `base`).
570:         .. note:: If either `base` or `height` are provided, both must be provided.
571:     ax : matplotlib.pyplot.axes
572:         An axis handle on which to draw the segmentation.
573:         If none is provided, a new set of axes is created.
574:     text_kw : dict
575:         If `labels` is provided, the properties of the text
576:         objects can be specified here.
577:         See `matplotlib.pyplot.Text` for valid parameters
578:     prop_cycle : cycle.Cycler
579:         An optional property cycle object to specify style properties.
580:         If not provided, the default property cycler will be retrieved from matplotlib.
581:     **kwargs
582:         Additional keyword arguments to pass to
583:         `matplotlib.pyplot.vlines`.
584: 
585:     Returns
586:     -------
587:     ax : matplotlib.pyplot.axes._subplots.AxesSubplot
588:         A handle to the (possibly constructed) plot axes
589:     """
590:     if text_kw is None:
591:         text_kw = dict()
592:     text_kw.setdefault("va", "top")
593:     text_kw.setdefault("clip_on", True)
594:     text_kw.setdefault("bbox", dict(boxstyle="round", facecolor="white"))
595: 
596:     # make sure we have an array for times
597:     times = np.asarray(times)
598: 
599:     # Get the axes handle
600:     ax, new_axes = __get_axes(ax=ax)
601: 
602:     if prop_cycle is None:
603:         __AXMAP[ax].setdefault("prop_cycle", mpl.rcParams["axes.prop_cycle"])
604:         __AXMAP[ax].setdefault("prop_iter", iter(mpl.rcParams["axes.prop_cycle"]))
605:     elif "prop_iter" not in __AXMAP[ax]:
606:         __AXMAP[ax]["prop_cycle"] = prop_cycle
607:         __AXMAP[ax]["prop_iter"] = iter(prop_cycle)
608: 
609:     prop_cycle = __AXMAP[ax]["prop_cycle"]
610:     prop_iter = __AXMAP[ax]["prop_iter"]
611: 
612:     if base is None and height is None:
613:         # If neither are provided, we'll use axes coordinates to span the figure
614:         base, height = 0, 1
615:         transform = ax.get_xaxis_transform()
616: 
617:     elif base is not None and height is not None:
618:         # If both are provided, we'll use data coordinates
619:         transform = None
620:     else:
621:         raise ValueError("When specifying base or height, both must be provided.")
622: 
623:     # Advance the property iterator if we can, restart it if we must
624:     try:
625:         properties = next(prop_iter)
626:     except StopIteration:
627:         prop_iter = iter(prop_cycle)
628:         __AXMAP[ax]["prop_iter"] = prop_iter
629:         properties = next(prop_iter)
630: 
631:     style = {
632:         k: v for k, v in properties.items() if k in ["color", "linestyle", "linewidth"]
633:     }
634:     style.update(kwargs)
635: 
636:     # If the user provided 'colors', don't override it with 'color'
637:     if "colors" in style:
638:         style.pop("color", None)
